chapters.title: Chapter 6: Landmark—Ciminelli v. United States and the Property Requirement
chapters.reason: This chapter directly teaches Ciminelli's holding rejecting the right-to-control theory and defining the 'property' requirement for federal fraud. Excerpts from the opinion are needed to show the Court's language on traditional property interests, to support model jury instructions, charging memoranda, and appellate reasoning about what qualifies as 'property' under fraud statutes.

chapters.title: Chapter 7: Landmark—Kousisis v. United States and the Fraudulent-Inducement Theory
chapters.reason: Kousisis is the Supreme Court endorsement of the fraudulent‑inducement theory and clarifies 'obtaining money or property' and the absence of a net‑pecuniary‑loss requirement. Direct excerpts are needed to explain the Court's framework, illustrative holdings, and to ground exercises on charging and defenses.

chapters.title: Chapter 8: Fifth Circuit Guideposts—Greenlaw, Evans, and Baker
chapters.reason: This chapter synthesizes Fifth Circuit precedent (Greenlaw, Evans, Baker) that defines §1348 elements—scheme, 'in connection with,' and intent—and the Fifth Circuit's approach to loss/gain issues. Including key excerpts will materially aid teaching how these cases are applied in charging, jury instructions, and circuit‑specific briefing.
